claim: Amazon ElastiCache is a web service for setting up, managing and scaling a distributed in-memory data store or cache in the cloud.
question: What is Amazon ElastiCache?

values.display: distributed in-memory data store or cache

evidence.quote: Amazon ElastiCache is a web service that makes it easy to set up, manage, and scale a distributed in-memory data store or cache environment in the cloud.

claim: Amazon ElastiCache works with the Valkey, Memcached and Redis OSS engines.
question: Which engines does Amazon ElastiCache work with?

values.display: Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS engines

evidence.quote: Amazon ElastiCache works with the Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS engines.

claim: You can operate ElastiCache in two formats: a serverless cache or a node-based cluster.
question: In which formats can you run ElastiCache?

evidence.quote: You can operate Amazon ElastiCache in two formats. You can get started with a serverless cache or create a node-based cluster.

claim: ElastiCache Serverless runs Valkey, Memcached or Redis OSS in cluster mode and is only compatible with clients that support TLS.
question: What must a client support to connect to an ElastiCache Serverless cache?

evidence.quote: ElastiCache Serverless runs Valkey, Memcached, or Redis OSS in cluster mode and is only compatible with clients that support TLS.

claim: ElastiCache Serverless automatically stores data redundantly across three Availability Zones.
question: How does ElastiCache Serverless store data for availability?

evidence.quote: ElastiCache Serverless automatically stores data redundantly across three Availability Zones and provides a 99.99% availability Service Level Agreement (SLA).

claim: ElastiCache Serverless automatically replicates your data across multiple Availability Zones for high availability, and it automatically monitors the underlying cache nodes and replaces them when they fail.
question: What does ElastiCache Serverless do for high availability and failed nodes?

values.display: replicates your data across multiple Availability Zones
replaces them in case of failures

evidence.quote: ElastiCache Serverless automatically replicates your data across multiple Availability Zones (AZ) for high-availability. It automatically monitors the underlying cache nodes and replaces them in case of failures.

claim: ElastiCache Serverless removes the need to plan and manage caching capacity. It monitors memory, compute and network bandwidth used by your application and scales to meet its needs.
question: Do you plan capacity for ElastiCache Serverless?

values.display: removes the need to plan and manage caching capacity

evidence.quote: ElastiCache Serverless also removes the need to plan and manage caching capacity. ElastiCache constantly monitors the cache’s memory, compute, and network bandwidth used by your application, and scales to meet the needs of your application.

claim: An ElastiCache Serverless cache handles all connections through a proxy layer, so the client does not need to rediscover the cluster topology when the underlying cluster changes.
question: Why does a serverless cache client need no topology rediscovery?

values.display: does not need to rediscover cluster topology

evidence.quote: When you request a new connection to the endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless handles all cache connections through a proxy layer. The proxy layer helps reduce complex client configuration, because the client does not need to rediscover cluster topology in case of changes to the underlying cluster.

claim: Backups from Valkey or Redis OSS node-based clusters can be restored into a serverless cache, and backups from serverless Valkey or Redis OSS caches can be restored into a node-based cluster.
question: Can a node-based Valkey or Redis OSS backup be restored into a serverless cache, and the other way round?

evidence.quote: Backups from Valkey or Redis OSS node-based clusters can be restored into a serverless configuration.
Backups from serverless Valkey or Redis OSS caches can be restored into a node-based cluster.

claim: AWS says to choose serverless caching for workloads that are new or difficult to predict and for unpredictable application traffic.
question: When should you choose ElastiCache Serverless over a node-based cluster?

evidence.quote: You are creating a cache for workloads that are either new or difficult to predict.
You have unpredictable application traffic.

claim: AWS says to create your own node-based cluster when you expect relatively predictable traffic and want fine-grained control over performance, availability and cost, and when you can forecast capacity requirements.
question: When should you choose a node-based cluster over ElastiCache Serverless?

evidence.quote: You expect your application traffic to be relatively predictable, and you want fine-grained control over performance, availability, and cost.
You can forecast your capacity requirements to control costs.

claim: When you create a node-based cluster, you are responsible for choosing the type and number of nodes so that the cache has enough capacity for your application.
question: Who is responsible for sizing a node-based ElastiCache cluster?

values.display: you are responsible for choosing the type and number of nodes
enough capacity as required by your application

evidence.quote: When creating a node-based cluster, you are responsible for choosing the type and number of nodes correctly to ensure that your cache has enough capacity as required by your application.

claim: In a node-based cluster you can run Valkey or Redis OSS in cluster mode by creating a cluster with multiple shards, or in non-cluster mode with a single shard.
question: How many shards does a node-based Valkey or Redis OSS cluster have in cluster mode and in non-cluster mode?

values.display: non-cluster mode with a single shard

qualifiers.scope: node-based Valkey or Redis OSS clusters

evidence.quote: You can choose to operate Valkey or Redis OSS in cluster mode by creating a cluster with multiple shards, or in non-cluster mode with a single shard.

claim: A node-based cluster can run with single-AZ availability or multi-AZ availability, depending on your needs.
question: Can a node-based ElastiCache cluster run in one Availability Zone or in several?

evidence.quote: For example, you can choose to operate a cluster with single-AZ availability or multi-AZ availability depending on your needs.

claim: You can take an ElastiCache backup at any time or set up automatic backups, and you can use a backup to restore an existing cache or to seed a new cache.
question: What can an ElastiCache backup be used for?

qualifiers.scope: serverless caches and Valkey or Redis OSS node-based clusters
qualifiers.condition: Valkey and Redis OSS node-based clusters, and serverless caches

evidence.quote: ElastiCache enables you to take a backup of your data at any time or setup automatic backups. Backups can be used to restore an existing cache or to seed a new cache.

claim: For node-based Valkey clusters, version 9.0 and higher, you can enable durability to persist your data in a Multi-AZ transactional log.
question: Which ElastiCache clusters can enable durability?

evidence.quote: For node-based Valkey clusters (version 9.0 and higher), you can enable durability to persist your data in a Multi-AZ transactional log.

note: Durability is a recent feature; see the durability change facts of the numbers lens.

claim: With durability enabled on a node-based Valkey cluster, data is protected even if all cache nodes fail, and replicas recover independently without impacting primary node performance.
question: What does durability protect against on a node-based Valkey cluster?

values.display: even if all cache nodes fail

qualifiers.scope: node-based Valkey clusters with durability enabled

evidence.quote: With durability enabled, your data is protected even if all cache nodes fail, and replicas recover independently without impacting primary node performance.
